title: When AI Spending Meets the Cash-Flow Test
intro: The Nasdaq's decline is not yet an all-stock crash. A few large companies and capital-intensive AI stories are being repriced, while many smaller US shares advanced. For your existing portfolio, the urgent question is whether a holding's earnings or financing changed, not whether its ticker moved with tech.

sections.label: Act 1 — AI is selling more; the cash bill is still due
sections.text: Good revenue growth and investable free cash flow are different things.
paragraphs: Amazon's original Q3 results reported AWS sales up 39.3%, but its issuer-defined free cash flow for the quarter was negative $33.456 billion: $42.422 billion operating cash flow less $75.878 billion net cash capital investment. The trailing-twelve-month free-cash-flow figure was negative $42.357 billion. The two periods must not be mixed.

Intel reported a stronger third quarter, but a $15–16 billion fourth-quarter sales outlook and weaker PC demand complicated the recovery. Sandisk's stronger data-centre numbers faced high expectations and a broad technology repricing. These are three different reasons to be cautious, not three proofs that AI demand collapsed.

Power Stack implication: MU, CRDO, AVGO, DELL and high-multiple grid suppliers require current valuations, customer funding proof and sustained issuer cash conversion. TSMC's strong earlier results are supportive of demand, not an automatic entry price.

sections.label: Act 2 — The Nasdaq headline hid a rotation
sections.text: Investors were repricing market leadership, not indiscriminately liquidating every company.
paragraphs: Bluebelly's source-dated 29 October breadth review saw 406 S&P constituents advancing against 97 declining, while an equal-weight S&P proxy gained about 1.20% and the cap-weighted proxy fell about 0.38%. Russell 2000 also rose. The observed split matters for the RSP versus concentrated-tech watch, but is not yet a multiweek breadth confirmation.

The 28 October available broad high-yield option-adjusted spread was about 3.14%, below 3.18% a session earlier. Because this credit observation predates the 29 October stock-session close, it argues against declaring an already-confirmed broad high-yield crisis; it does not guarantee credit remained calm into the Amazon after-hours shock.

Power Stack should distinguish a sell-off driven by inflated share-price expectations from one where financing covenants, default risk or customers' willingness to pay have deteriorated. An AI data-centre customer and a profitable electrical equipment supplier need different underwriting.

sections.label: Act 3 — Sticky PCE, but bonds still rallied
sections.text: Inflation constrains the Fed without mechanically setting the next day's Treasury and dollar direction.
paragraphs: The BEA's September PCE report showed headline prices up 3.6% year over year and 0.5% month over month; core PCE rose 3.1% and 0.3%. These readings were largely in line with cited analyst expectations, but remain higher than the Fed's longer-run 2% objective. Nominal consumer outlays rose 0.5% while inflation-adjusted spending was essentially flat.

Bluebelly's reviewed 29 October yield comparison saw indicative 10-year Treasury yields fall from 5.05% to about 4.98% and 2-year yields fall from 4.67% to 4.61%. A separately sourced 10-year real-yield comparison also declined. Government duration may benefit from a growth/risk scare even when inflation is high.

For VGIT, IEF, TLT and a possible cash reserve, the unresolved issue is whether lower yields last and how MYR exchange rates affect returns. Do not confuse a Treasury rally with cheap borrowing for leveraged AI firms, and do not call DXY technically broken without a completed 4H/daily series.

sections.label: Act 4 — Japan and oil complicate the risk picture
sections.text: Physical energy and currency transmission are live questions, not completed investment verdicts.
paragraphs: The Bank of Japan held its policy rate at 1.25% by an 8–1 vote on 30 October, with one member favouring 1.50%. Its inflation projections and higher planned ETF disposal pace made the hold less straightforwardly dovish, but the ETF-sale change takes effect in January 2027. A weaker Nasdaq and falling US yields may also have contributed to yen strength; there is no verified completed carry-trade unwind.

Reuters' 30 October 03:23 UTC report distinguished expiring December Brent near $116.08 from January Brent near $112.19. They are different contracts, not evidence of a $3.89 intraday fall. UKMTO's ship-incident description and subsequent reporting differed on the weapon; neither proves the exact cargo or lost barrels.

For your XOM, HIBISCS and MISC positions, keep integrated production/refining, upstream cash generation and contracted maritime/LNG earnings separate. YTLPOWR and TENAGA demand forecasts also need customer/funding proof rather than a generic 'AI infrastructure beneficiary' label.

sections.label: Act 5 — What I'd review with the existing RM13,491
sections.text: Before rotating capital, understand the risks already owned.
paragraphs: Your eight recorded holdings have not changed. First validate YTL-linked warrant 6742UW's actual strike, expiry, bid/ask and cost; then reassess YTLPOWR's portfolio concentration and funded AI/data-centre economics; review DAYANG's operating recovery and whether capital remains justified; and check Tesla's earnings/cash/SpaceX-related terms on issuer filings. These are review priorities, not forced sale orders.

The energy cluster (XOM, HIBISCS, MISC) must be tested against realised prices, volumes, refined margins and physical shipping evidence. TTWO deserves its own bookings/release-catalyst analysis instead of a blanket AI-market call. Diversifying into CF, VGIT/IEF, RSP or grid suppliers still requires current security prices, liquidity and a costed MYR funding plan.

The RM13,491 mandate describes total starting risk capital—not an additional RM13,491 cash balance. Historical holdings quotes mostly dated 21–22 October, unverified warrant price, missing XOM/warrant cost and unknown brokerage cash block an executable NAV-weighted rebalance. No positions, company scores, targets or orders were changed by this market-summary update.

verdict: Current personal-investment verdict: review existing capital before adding AI risk. Prioritise 6742UW contract terms, YTLPOWR concentration and fundamentals, DAYANG operating thesis and TSLA cash/valuation; keep energy exposures distinct. The last completed US session showed selective AI repricing and broadening breadth, not a verified general credit meltdown. No order without current exchange price, issuer evidence, FX/broker cash and a written invalidation.

introParagraphs: On 29 October, the Nasdaq Composite declined roughly 1.4%, but Russell 2000 rose about 1% and a Bluebelly breadth review counted 406 S&P 500 advancers against 97 decliners. That is a genuine split between headline index performance and underlying participation; one day cannot prove a durable rotation.

September PCE inflation remains above the Fed's target. Meanwhile, 29 October US Treasury yields fell and the dollar weakened, so it would be wrong to assert that every inflation warning must lift yields or DXY immediately. Bluebelly's 30 October Asia observations are intraday, not a 30 October US closing signal.
